classification.difficultyReason: Use equal building heights to interpret the depression angles, find the sightline and horizontal separation, then calculate the total height and subtract the antenna height.

content.prompt: A 12 m high antenna is on top of a building $BC$. Opposite the road is another building $DE$ with the same height. From the top of the antenna, the angles of depression to the base and top of building $DE$ respectively are $70^\circ$ and $30^\circ$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 3 shared antenna and buildings diagram
spec.description: A, B and C lie on the left vertical; D and E lie on the right vertical. B and E are level, as are C and D. AB has an external 12 m dimension arrow. Solid outlines include AC, CD, DE and the short roof extending right from E. BE, AE and AD are dashed. A dashed horizontal arrow extends right from A, and C has a right-angle square. Both depression angles are measured from the horizontal through A. Geometry uses the stated angles rather than the source's schematic proportions. All marks are black and unshaded.
spec.mathematics: AB=12 m, BC=DE, horizontal-to-AE depression 30°, horizontal-to-AD depression 70°. The angle between AE and AD is not labelled 70°.
spec.answerVisibility: No calculated distances or building heights are visible.

answer.worked:
The equal building heights make $BE$ horizontal, so $\angle AEB=30^\circ$. In right-angled $\triangle ABE$,
$$\begin{align*}\sin30^\circ&=\frac{12}{AE}\\AE&=\frac{12}{\sin30^\circ}\\AE&=24\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the height of building $BC$, correct to the nearest metre.

answer.worked:
The horizontal separation is $CD=BE$.
$$\begin{align*}CD&=24\cos30^\circ\\CD&=12\sqrt3\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
The angle of elevation $\angle ADC$ is $70^\circ$. In right-angled $\triangle ACD$,
$$\begin{align*}AC&=CD\tan70^\circ\\AC&=12\sqrt3\tan70^\circ\text{ m}\\BC&=AC-AB\\BC&=12\sqrt3\tan70^\circ-12\text{ m}\\BC&\approx45.11\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
The building is $45\text{ m}$ high, to the nearest metre.
